category_title: Students with persistent challenging behavior referred for individualized support
minimal_context: The student is participating in a large group reading instruction activity where the class is asked to read from their textbooks.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Everyone, please open your reading books to page 12 so we can read the next chapter together.

STUDENT: (Puts head down on desk and starts making inappropriate vocalizations while the rest of the group opens their books.)

TUTOR: Please sit up and open your book to page 12.

STUDENT: (Leaves seat without permission, walks over to the student at the next desk, and starts touching their reading materials.)

TUTOR: Go back to your seat and leave their things alone.

STUDENT: (Shouts above the current conversational level) I'm not going back! (Takes the peer's reading materials without permission and drops them on the floor.)

options.A: Provide a clear beginning and end for the current reading task.
options.B: Call on a neighboring student, ask a peer, or poll the class for help.
options.C: Agree with the student that they are having a rough time right now.
options.D: Provide an opportunity to respond as a form of teacher attention.
